A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WhiSPA study. All 13 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original WTC and HiTOP experiments, psychological prediction results, loss-function comparisons and evaluation on human-annotated speech segments in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline and teacher-model results, plus correlations between linguistic features and model predictions.

M1.justification: The backbone, teachers, pooling, psychological augmentation variants and loss formulas are retained. However, v1 describes pooling after predicting <EOT> and calls temperature trainable; v2 states non-autoregressive operation with precomputed transcripts and calls temperature tunable, set to 0.1. The PDFs do not establish whether these are procedural changes or corrections to the description.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WTC and HiTOP interviews, ten self-supervised psychological dimensions, eleven person-level outcomes and 300 human-annotated segments. Figure 8's arousal results concern an existing self-supervised task; the new linguistic analysis reuses WTC.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 replace Wav2Vec-768 with Wav2Vec2-BERT and add HuBERT, retaining Whisper-384. Table 2 additionally evaluates SBERT-384, previously compared only in Table 5. Figure 8 adds standalone PsychEmb-10 predictions. These substantially broaden and revise the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 adds a procedure correlating WTC n-grams with predicted PCL scores and selecting the strongest positive and negative associations for comparison with Whisper (Table 6). The existing split, ten-fold ridge evaluation, annotation sample and training budget remain unchanged. Clearer person-level pooling descriptions do not establish a changed evaluation.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.4 add a focused interpretability study of linguistic features associated with WTC PTSD predictions, reported in Table 6. The existing loss-function, replacement-versus-projection, SBERT-augmentation and latent-overlap analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 6 introduces Benjamini–Hochberg-corrected significance reporting for n-gram correlations. Existing paired t-tests and p < .05 reporting remain. Neither version reports additional training runs, seeds or uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Shared Whisper and WhiSPA numerical entries in Tables 2–5 are unchanged, but comparator, teacher and n-gram results substantially expand the evidence. HuBERT now leads HiTOP extraversion at r = .77, above the previously leading WhiSPA-394 at .72. New Figure 8 also conflicts with retained Table 3: Whisper disinhibition is plotted as .53 rather than .33, and WhiSPA-394 thought disorder as .39 rather than .37.

T1.justification: The cosine-similarity and NCE equations and associated mathematical definitions are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theoretical propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: V2 foregrounds novelty in the alignment objective and adds an explicit first-work claim for semantic/psychological cross-modal enrichment of a foundational speech model at the end of Section 2. The central accuracy, contrastive-learning and redundant-SBERT conclusions already appear in v1; emphasizing pipeline efficiency does not introduce a new capability claim.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new linguistic associations as evidence of sensitivity to distress and self-reference, and suggests positive-affect or relationship language could indicate resilience relevant to screening. Appendix A.4 also connects arousal to teacher-limited acoustic preservation. General concerns about lexical bias and teacher capacity were already present in v1.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the new baseline checkpoints, explicitly documents precomputed training transcripts and clarifies person-level pooling for Table 2. It removes v1's explicit statement that Tables 2–3 use NCE-trained models. Appendix A.2's hyperparameters, hardware and training time, and the code/data access statements, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially replaces general model background with positioning against multimodal fusion, acoustic-to-text approaches and cross-modal distillation. Added discussions include Zhao et al. (2022), Chen et al. (2021), Dong et al. (2022) and Wu et al. (2024), alongside a rationale for choosing Whisper and an explicit priority claim. Several earlier background citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, conclusion and limitations are extensively rewritten around avoiding a subsequent text language model. Results discussion is reorganized and Appendix A.4 is added. V2 also introduces visibly unfinished introductory prose, including 'repdirect speech(??)'.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from overlapping latent spaces to a pipeline diagram; Figure 2 is redrawn with clearer component labels and relocated. V2 adds Figure 8 and two-panel Table 6, expands and restructures Tables 2–3, reverses Table 3's dataset column order, and revises table grouping and captions. Existing appendix figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation breadth and research positioning through broader comparisons and a new linguistic analysis. However, its new Figure 8 contradicts unchanged Table 3 on two reported correlations, while the introduction contains unfinished text. These additions improve coverage but introduce material reporting and editorial defects, leaving the net change in overall quality uncertain.
